text:
jamie_support: Heads-up: Acme Transport (tenant acme-transport) opened an urgent ticket — DELETE /v1/objects/obj-9a7d returns 202 but the object is still returned by GET. Regulator asking for proof of deletion. Escalating for retention/KMS/audit guidance. Req: req_ab12cd
acme_billing: customer says they sent two delete requests earlier today and still sees data. this is blocking their compliance sign-off.
eli_infra: can you paste the exact curl + response headers and the request id so I can trace in storage?
jamie_support: curl they used:
```
curl -X DELETE "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/objects/obj-9a7d" \\ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_redacted" \\ 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json"
```
response body: empty, status 202
response headers:
```
Request-Id: req_ab12cd
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 4987
```
jamie_support: infra excerpt (sanitized):
```
2026-07-12T09:41:02Z INFO delete-request id=obj-9a7d tenant=acme-transport req=req_ab12cd
2026-07-12T09:41:02Z INFO retention-mark id=obj-9a7d policy=tenant-default-90d
2026-07-12T09:41:02Z INFO audit event created actor=acme.user@example.com action=delete_requested obj=obj-9a7d
```
anna_security: tagging @eli_infra @maria_engineer. Recap: our API accepts delete and transitions object to soft-deleted state; actual physical removal follows retention TTL (tenant default 90 days) unless customer has a contractual immediate-erasure SLA or legal-authorized expedited purge. Also note: backups and object store snapshots may keep bytes longer. KMS keys remain unless key destruction requested separately. :lock:
maria_engineer: implementation note: GET behavior can vary — some read-paths exclude soft-deleted objects, others surface them with metadata until hard-delete. We need to know which route the customer used. Also check whether object was part of an immutable backup/snapshot (e.g., nightly archive).
acme_billing: customer insists they never set a custom retention. they need a formal retention statement and a deletion ETA or proof of purge.
eli_infra: storage trace: object moved to delete-queue retention_until=2026-10-10T09:41:02Z (90d). No active snapshot references found in last scan, but weekly backups could include it. Audit line (raw):
```
2026-07-12T09:41:02Z tenant=acme-transport actor=acme.user@example.com action=delete_requested object=obj-9a7d req=req_ab12cd
```
anna_security: questions to resolve now:
- Confirm tenant retention override exists? (jamie to ask customer)
- Find backups/snapshot indexes that might contain the object after delete request (eli)
- Advise on KMS effects and whether key destruction requested (ops_runbook)

jamie_support: Acme confirms no custom retention on their side. they are preparing a signed, regulator-facing erasure request.
maria_engineer: if we get signed erasure + legal approval we can initiate an expedited purge. high-level runbook: 1) legal approves and logs decision, 2) ops runs purge-job targeting primary stores, 3) ops issues best-effort requests to long-term backup system owners to remove from archives where feasible, 4) generate signed deletion receipt. Note: cannot guarantee removal from external cold backups depending on provider retention; we will document scope.
ops_runbook: purge-job details: it atomically deletes live object, strips metadata, writes audit entry, and emits a signed deletion receipt. backups: we mark deletion in backup-index and request removal; physical bytes in some immutable archives may remain until archive retention expires. Estimated time for primary purge: 24-72 hours after legal approval; backup cleanup: variable (days-weeks) depending on archive policies.
acme_billing: timeframe is helpful — customer needs a dated confirmation they can present to regulator.
eli_infra: when we run purge, we'll include an ops request id and audit entries like:
```
{"object":"obj-9a7d","deleted_at":"2026-07-14T12:03:55Z","method":"expedited_purge","ops_req":"ops_purge_20260714_7"}
```
jamie_support: noted. I'm sending the customer the legal authorization template and will post their signed form here when we receive it. tagging @anna_security for compliance.
acme_billing: customer will send signed erasure form EOD. they asked whether destroying tenant CMK will help — they want to know if that would make archived blobs unreadable.
anna_security: CMK destruction is a separate legal/ops process and has wide implications (affects all ciphertext for this tenant). We need legal signoff and platform ops coordination; key destruction is irreversible and must be approached carefully. If customer only needs PII purge, we should prefer object-level purge and document remaining ciphertext risk.
jamie_support: created INC-20260712-88 and escalated to ops. I'll update this thread with attachments: signed erasure form, legal approval, and the deletion receipt once purge completes.
auditbot: Audit link: https://audit.redwood.ai/tenants/acme-transport/entries?req=req_ab12cd
jamie_support: summary for the record: default retention = 90 days. we cannot bypass without signed erasure + legal. with approvals, primary-store purge ETA ~24-72h; backup/archive cleanup best-effort and subject to archive provider TTLs. will post deletion receipt once completed.
acme_billing: thanks — customer expects proof and will push legal side. please flag any blockers.
anna_security: acknowledged. keep timestamps and receipts in-thread. once purge completes, attach the signed deletion receipt and the ops audit id. :white_check_mark:
